findings.text: deferred_remainder re-implements the two computations its immediate neighbours already own: the declarations-present guard and plan_executable_remainder == 0 test are is_closable (reckon/roadmap.py:958-985) copied verbatim, and the deferred-section filter dictating SECTION_DECLARATION_DEFERRED is a fourth copy of the idiom closure_blockers already runs at reckon/roadmap.py:1010-1022 (see also roadmap.py:730 and :774). Calling is_closable and reading the section entries out of closure_blockers would give one owner. The copy matters here rather than being stylistic: the guard carries a comment in is_closable explaining why an absent declaration set must not read as resolved, and a second copy has no such warning attached, so a future change to that reading drifts silently: the review search over the capability found is_closable and closure_blockers in the same module, and none was extended.

The bar's done-share is still drawn from flowDonePercent(item) over the served split, which for a plan at impl 1.0 covers the whole span, so the crew flow still paints a fully finished bar at the now line for exactly the plan this change targets; only the text label at docs/ui/crew.jsx:155 changes. The plan section's complaint was the finished bar attached to the now line as much as the figure, so the surface now states two different things about the same plan.

The surface guard is a source-text check: asserting 'deferred_remainder' appears in the JSX passes on a mention anywhere in the file, so deleting the render at docs/ui/crew.jsx:139 or docs/ui/shell-plans.jsx:690 while leaving the identifier in a comment keeps the assertion green. It fails on the obvious regression (removing both) but not on the one it was added to prevent, which is a surface that stops rendering the served fact.

The evidence fence requires that every test file importing a production module the node changed adds no failure against a base arm; the importer population (112 files importing reckon.roadmap or reckon.serve) was run on neither arm to a summary, so that clause is unmeasured rather than satisfied. The worker records this honestly at manifest.md:24 and :26 and did not widen the node to cover it, but a reader must not read the gate's 28 passed as covering the population: an added row key can redden a test elsewhere that compares a row dict for equality.
